feedback:
Decision: approve. The candidate is identical to iteration 6, the best raced design (85.60). Its sensor spread is reverted from the iteration 8 test (±0.08 m, rejected because it cut the oval to 0.2039 progress and collapsed s-bend and slalom). The only other evidence needed is that iteration 6 is the best design raced so far, so this is a reproduction and not a new gamble. Approving it banks a known score this iteration, and the iteration 8 result shows that widening the span can hurt sharply.

No outcome is claimed for this race. The expectation is near 85.6, with oval line losses at 0 and oval progress near 0.34, as in iteration 6. Oval max_error (about 0.062, from iteration 6) and the single line loss each on s-bend and slalom (every recovery direction and speed tried so far, iterations 0 to 6) are still open problems.

What to do with the next iteration, depending on what this race shows:
(a) If the race reproduces about 85.6, the controller and sensing are stable. The next test should move one lever at a time. The best-supported untested lever is base_speed. Speed 1.4 gave oval progress 0.137, 1.2 gave 0.318 and 1.0 gave 0.3425, so the gain is flattening but not finished. Try base_speed 0.9 with all else at iteration 6 values, and keep it only if oval progress holds and oval max_error drops below 0.06.
(b) If the race falls well below 85.6, the cause is probably run-to-run variance on the oval. Do not change the sensors again. Revisit kd only with a small step (0.25) and check that progress stays near 0.34.
(c) Leave the fifth forward sensor idea for later. Weight-0 sensors dilute the reading sum, and iteration 8 shows sensing changes can hurt sharply, so that test should only run if the speed test has stalled.
